sources.entry: Cal.diy - Online appointment scheduling system. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs
Cal.diy | Open-source scheduling platform from Cal.com, a Calendly alternative

summary.one_liner: Cal.diy is the MIT-licensed, self-hosted community edition of Cal.com, an online appointment scheduling platform built on Next.js and PostgreSQL.
summary.what_it_does: Cal.diy is a fork of Cal.com with enterprise and commercial code removed, so it has no license key and no Teams, Organizations, Insights, Workflows, or SSO/SAML features. It runs on your own infrastructure, with Node.js 18+ and PostgreSQL 13+ as prerequisites, and Prisma manages the database schema. The README describes a local development setup using Yarn, a `yarn dx` Docker-based quick start with seeded test users, and manual setup with a `.env` file. Deployment is documented via Docker Compose (prebuilt image on DockerHub or building from source), with notes on Railway, Northflank, Vercel, Render and Elestio. Optional integrations with Google Calendar, Microsoft Graph, Zoom, Daily.co, Basecamp, HubSpot, ZohoCRM and others are configured through OAuth credentials in `.env`. Rate limiting via Unkey and a Content Security Policy option are also mentioned as optional.
use_cases: replace Calendly with a self-hosted tool
booking links for meetings and calls
run a scheduling app on my own server
Google Calendar and Zoom booking integration
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd into cal.diy
Copy .env.example to .env and set NEXTAUTH_SECRET and CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (openssl rand -base64 32 / 24)
yarn dx (requires Docker and Docker Compose; starts local Postgres with test users)
Or deploy with: docker compose up -d
notable: MIT-licensed with no enterprise or commercial code split, unlike Cal.com's open-core model
Docker Compose stack bundles Postgres, the web app and Prisma Studio
Quick start with yarn dx seeds sample free, pro, trial and admin users
Setup wizard on first Docker run creates the first user
Optional integrations are documented step by step with OAuth redirect URIs
caveats: README says it is strictly recommended for personal, non-production use and requires advanced server administration knowledge
Vercel deployment requires the Vercel Pro Plan due to serverless function limits on the free plan
Building from source with Docker requires an available database during the build and DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0
keywords: let people book time with me
